why: Each case is an input that a render-time sanitiser, or a strip-after-NFC order, or a UTF-16 cap would get wrong. `stored` is what the DB must hold.

cases.why: EC-SEC-01: a report note with RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE reorders the Settings rows around it, and reaches a GitHub issue verbatim when the learner consents.
cases.stored: audio is wrong gnorw si oidua

cases.why: EC-GRD-24: a pasted ZERO WIDTH SPACE inside an otherwise exact answer. Grading must not see it and the solution banner must not render it.
Strip must run BEFORE NFC: a ZWNJ between the base letter and its combining mark blocks composition, so a normalise-first order stores the decomposed form and grading misses an exact answer.
EC-SEC-06: 40,000 pasted characters. The cap is in code points and the field cap is 500.
A cap counted in UTF-16 units would cut the 500th parrot in half and store a lone surrogate one step after the strip removed them.
A BOM and a FIRST STRONG ISOLATE hidden in a tier-3 diff. Cf is stripped by category, not by a hand-written list.
Whitespace controls are Cc but must become spaces, not vanish with the rest of the class.
